title: Review: Cathay Pacific First Class on Boeing 777-300ER - Hong Kong to New York
summary: Cathay Pacific's First Class seats on the Boeing 777-300ER made for a comfortable long-haul flight from Hong Kong to New York.
body_markdown:
A more than 15-hour travel day isn’t as bad when you’re flying First Class with


[Cathay Pacific](https://roame.travel/guides/cathay-a330-business-class-review-hkg-tpe) .


I recently flew on the airline’s Boeing 777-300ER nonstop from Hong Kong (HKG) to New York (JFK). While First Class on Cathay Pacific is quite dated, the service, food, and drinks are still top-notch. The seats were spacious, the pajamas were unexpectedly comfortable, and the multi-course meal made for a delightful dining experience.


Cathay Pacific's First Class seat on the Boeing 777-300ER flight from Hong Kong (HKG) to New York (JFK).


## **Cathay Pacific First Class Price**


Long-haul first class flights are notoriously expensive, and Cathay Pacific’s can cost more than $17,000 one-way or $30,000 round-trip.


However, I was able to book two Cathay Pacific First Class flights for only 125,000 miles each.


The Asia-based airline will occasionally release large blocks of award flight availability in business and first class. To save me time, I had


[Roame](https://roame.travel/) alerts set for flights between the United States and Hong Kong. These alerts comb through airlines’ reward flight availability to help you find the deals as they're released.


Roame alerts for Cathay Pacific flights from the United States to Hong Kong.


I ended up using one of Roame's email and text alerts to book my Hong Kong to New York flight for only 160,000


****


Cathay Pacific points, plus $146 in taxes.


You can also use the


[Roame Cathay Pacific finder](https://roame.travel/programs/cathay) for quick access.


## **Cathay Pacific’s The Pier, First Class Lounge at Hong Kong International Airport (HKG)**


Your journey begins before you board the plane: After a trek through the busy airport, a stop at Cathay Pacific’s The Pier, First Class Lounge is a must-do.


Located near Gate 63 in Terminal 1 of Hong Kong International Airport (HKG), the lounge evokes a spa-like atmosphere with dark walnut wood and soft lighting. Amenities include massage treatments, private day suites, showers, a cocktail bar, and workstations.


Cathay Pacific’s The Pier, First Class Lounge at Hong Kong International Airport.


It's a popular destination: The sit-down dining room was packed, and there was a line to wait for a table.


If you’re arriving with a business class ticket in hand, make sure to head to the flagship


[Cathay Pacific The Pier, Business Class Lounge](https://roame.travel/guides/cathay-pacific-the-pier-business-class-lounge-review-HKG) instead.


## **Cathay Pacific’s First Class cabin and seats**


Cathay Pacific is widely regarded as one of the best Asian airlines. However, while the service, meal, and drinks were impeccable, the cabin could use a refresh. The last major update for the first class seats was in 2013, nearly 13 years ago.


A First Class seat on Cathay Pacific's Boeing 777-300ER flight.


There were only six first class seats in a 1-1-1 seat configuration, each at a spacious 36 inches wide and 81 inches long.


Cathay Pacific's First Class seats on the Boeing 777-300ER had impeccable service, food, and drinks, despite a dated design.


I booked seat 1A by the window, which was configured away from the aisle for more seclusion. Several pillows padded my seats, and the deep footwell let me stretch out. There was a designated literature storage cubby, and the USB-A and power outlets were conveniently located within arm’s reach.


Cathay Pacific's First Class seats are equipped with USB and power-A outlets.


Cathay Pacific's First Class seats come with literature storage pockets.


That being said, the cabin looked quite worn down. The grey plastic and wood-grain accents showed the aircraft’s more than decade-old age and reminded me of American Airlines’ transcon first class seats. I’m looking forward to Cathay’s rumored new Halo First Class suites.


Luckily, the seats are extremely large and comfy.


## **Entertainment and amenities**


Cathay Pacific's First Class seats are equipped with 18.5-inch screens.


There’s a reason Cathay Pacific’s in-flight entertainment is award-winning. For starters, the provided Wilkins and Bowers noise-canceling headphones helped tune out the engine’s buzz. And the 18.5-inch screens came loaded with enough classic TV series, Asian and Hollywood films, podcasts, and even Disney+ programs to binge for the 15-hour-plus journey.


While there was free Wifi, it was spotty.


Cathay Pacific's Bamford amenity kit.


Cathay Pacific tapped British luxury lifestyle and wellness company, Bamford, for its amenity kits. The kit included a facial mist, a moisturizing balm, peppermint mouthwash, an eye mask, earplugs, and a toothbrush kit.


The lavatory was clean, but again dated and in need of a modern refresh.


## **Food and beverages**


Let’s start with the headline: I was served my own tin of Kaluga Queen caviar with blinis, chives, chopped eggs, and creme fraîche (of course). The fish eggs were the perfectly salty balance to the accompanying glass of 2004 Krug Vintage champagne


Cathay Pacific's signature caviar and champagne.


Overall, the white tablecloth dining program was a highlight of the flight. Flight attendants presented each course with individual plating, and I was quite surprised by how many dishes there were.


The exact options vary by flight, but for dinner, travelers can typically expect caviar, a Chinese or international main course, cheese, and dessert.


Wok-fried lobster in a white pepper sauce with green onions and ginger, served with a side of steamed vegetable-stuffed winter melon rolls.


The Hong Kong-based airline certainly does justice to its national cuisine. I was especially partial to the all-day menu’s plump wonton noodle soup and freshly steamed dim sum. The Chinese-style double-boiled chicken soup with coconut and yellow fungus mushroom was light but warming, while the traditional fish congee (served with accouterments such as peanuts and green onions) was hearty and nostalgic.


Chinese fish congee.


Chinese-style double-boiled chicken soup with coconut and yellow fungus mushrooms.


For breakfast, I had my pick of fresh juices and smoothies, seasonal fruit, cereals, baked goods, and vanilla yogurt with pomegranate molasses, fig, and raspberries.


## **Sleep experience**


When it was time to sleep, the flight attendant converted my suite into a bed with a plush mattress, 600-thread-count linen, a thick pillow, and a pillow mist.


The First Class seats turned into spacious and comfortable beds.


The pajamas from Hong Kong-based clothing brand Pye were amazing. They felt premium and comfortable enough to bring back home and wear.


The photos make the Cathay Pacific first class seats look deceptively small, but they're actually quite spacious. I slept for a wonderful six hours on board.


Pajamas and slippers designed by Pye.


## **Final thoughts on Cathay’s 777 First Class**


Despite the dated design, the comfortable pajamas, ultra-spacious seating, and excellent multi-course dinner made the more than 15-hour flight time feel more like a vacation than a transoceanic commute.


## **Overall Rating: 7/10**


My rating breakdown:


- Food Quality: 9/10


- Drinks Quality: 8/10


- Cleanliness: 7/10


- Cabin Design: 5/10


- Seat: 5/10


- Service: 9/10


Cathay Pacific’s Boeing 777-300ER First Class was well worth the 125,000 Cathay Pacific points, thanks to Roame’s convenient


[award search and alerts](https://roame.travel/subscription) .
